B02_00.process: Small RNA guided silencing of messenger RNAs after transcription.

B02_01.process: Keeping ribosomal RNA genes active to support ribosome production.
B02_01.disease: Cockayne syndrome, with growth failure and neurodegeneration.
B02_01.tissue: Most cell types, acting in the nucleolus.

B02_02.process: Epigenetic silencing of ribosomal RNA genes to limit ribosome production.
B02_02.tissue: Most cell types, acting in the nucleolus.

B02_03.process: Production of small interfering RNAs for RNA interference.
B02_03.disease: Antiviral defense; no specific disease named.

B02_04.process: Opening chromatin at ribosomal RNA gene promoters for transcription.
B02_04.tissue: Most cell types, acting in the nucleolus.

B02_05.process: Starting transcription of ribosomal RNA genes for ribosome production.
B02_05.tissue: Most cell types, especially proliferating cells.

B02_06.process: DNA methylation that maintains heritable gene silencing.
B02_06.tissue: Most cell types, notably embryos and germ cells.

B02_07.process: Polycomb histone methylation that maintains heritable gene silencing during development.
B02_07.tissue: Most cell types, especially developing and stem cells.

B02_08.process: Silencing transposable elements by building repressive chromatin.
B02_08.disease: Genome instability and innate immune activation.
B02_08.tissue: Most cell types, especially early embryos and germ cells.

B02_09.process: Making small RNAs that silence transposons in germ cells.
B02_09.tissue: Male germ cells in the testis.

B02_10.tissue: Germ cells, embryos, stem cells, neurons and blood stem cells.

B02_11.process: Assembly of histone-modifying complexes that activate gene transcription.
B02_11.disease: Kabuki and Wiedemann-Steiner syndromes and mixed lineage leukemia.
B02_11.tissue: Most cell types, especially developing embryonic tissues.

B02_12.process: Energy-dependent silencing of ribosomal RNA genes under nutrient stress.
B02_12.disease: Ageing and metabolic stress; no specific disease named.
B02_12.tissue: Most cell types, acting in the nucleolus.

B02_13.process: Production of microRNAs that regulate gene expression.

B02_14.process: Transcription of small structural RNAs by RNA polymerase III.
B02_14.disease: Hypomyelinating leukodystrophies, neurodevelopmental disease and cancer.

B02_15.process: Starting transcription of 5S ribosomal RNA for ribosome production.
B02_15.disease: Hypomyelinating leukodystrophies and impaired innate immunity.

B02_16.process: Ending transcription of ribosomal RNA genes.
B02_16.tissue: Most cell types, acting in the nucleolus.

B02_17.process: Silencing retrotransposons and foreign DNA by repressive chromatin.
B02_17.disease: Viral infection, including HIV, and genome instability.

B02_18.process: Chromatin remodelling that activates ribosomal RNA gene transcription.
B02_18.tissue: Most cell types, acting in the nucleolus.

B02_19.process: Ending transcription of small structural RNAs by RNA polymerase III.

B02_20.process: Stress-induced production of small RNAs from transfer RNAs.
B02_20.disease: Cellular stress responses and viral infection.

B02_21.process: Early transcription of small structural RNAs by RNA polymerase III.

B02_22.process: Starting transcription of small nuclear RNAs needed for splicing.

B02_23.process: Chromatin-coupled gene activation driving fat cell formation and lipid storage.
B02_23.disease: Fatty liver disease, steatohepatitis and cirrhosis.
B02_23.tissue: Fat cells, brown fat and liver cells.

B02_24.process: Small RNA guided control of gene transcription in the nucleus.

B02_25.process: Starting transcription of transfer RNAs by RNA polymerase III.

B02_26.process: Transition from initiation to elongation in ribosomal RNA transcription.
B02_26.tissue: Most cell types, acting in the nucleolus.

B02_27.process: Small RNA guided DNA methylation silencing transposons in germ cells.
B02_27.tissue: Male germ cells in the testis.
